title: Predictive scaling signal evaluation (candidate signals + scoring matrix)
content:
Sheet overview
- Purpose: shortlist predictive scaling inputs (signals) for Dedicated autoscaler “predictive mode” and rank by usefulness vs complexity.
- Output: (1) MVP signals, (2) phase-2 candidates, (3) signals to avoid (too complex/noisy/low coverage).
- Scope assumption: predictive signal is a bias/target for desired replicas; reactive loop can override when saturation/queue depth indicates we’re wrong; min/max bounds always clamp.

Definitions / notes
- “Lead time” = how far ahead the signal gives a meaningful heads-up vs purely reactive scaling. For Dedicated this is mostly about avoiding cold starts + queue buildup during known ramps.
- “Coverage” = % of Dedicated deployments where signal is available and meaningful.
- “Reliability” = stability + likelihood of being wrong in ways that cause harm (oscillation/overprovision).
- “Complexity” includes data pipeline work, model/logic, operational burden, customer config/support.

Scoring rubric (0–5)
- Usefulness score (U): 0 (no benefit) … 5 (material reduction in ramp latency / queueing)
- Complexity score (C): 0 (trivial) … 5 (very hard / high ops)
- Reliability score (R): 0 (unreliable) … 5 (highly reliable)
- Coverage score (V): 0 (rare) … 5 (broad)

Derived prioritization (for sorting)
- Priority index (PI) = (2*U + R + V) - (1.5*C)
  - Heavier weight on usefulness; penalize complexity.
  - Not meant to be perfect; mainly to compare candidates.

Tab: Candidate signals (table)
Columns: ID | Signal | Signal type | Data source | Granularity | Update freq | Expected lead time | Coverage (0-5) | Reliability (0-5) | Usefulness (0-5) | Complexity (0-5) | Priority index | Failure modes / risks | Implementation notes | MVP? (Y/N)

1 | Time-of-day / day-of-week seasonal baseline | Forecast (statistical) | Redwood request metrics (QPS/tokens), per deployment | deployment_id + region | daily retrain; 5–15m refresh | 15–120 min | 5 | 4 | 4 | 2 | 11.0 | Timezone misalignment; holidays; product launches | Start simple: per-deployment “seasonal profile” (DOW x 5-min buckets). Require customer timezone in config; default UTC with warning. | Y
2 | Scheduled events (customer-provided) | Explicit schedule | Console/API config (new field) | deployment_id | on change; evaluated continuously | 15–240 min (customer chooses) | 3 | 5 | 4 | 2 | 11.0 | Misconfigured schedules; config churn; wrong region | Requires clear UX + validation (no overlapping windows?); rate-limit config updates; show upcoming scheduled scale changes in UI. | Y
3 | Recent trend extrapolation (EMA on QPS/tokens) | Reactive-adjacent | Redwood request metrics | deployment_id + region | 1m | 5–15 min | 5 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 10.5 | Chases noise; can amplify spikes; may fight cooldown | This is “predictive-lite”; safe if bounded + dampened; should be default fallback when no long-horizon forecast. | Y (as fallback)
4 | Queue depth derivative / pre-queue signals | Leading indicator | Autoscaler telemetry + runtime queue metrics | deployment_id + replica | 10–30s | 1–5 min | 4 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 8.0 | Queue depth unstable for some models/batching; sensitive to traffic shape | Needs model-aware smoothing; may be better as reactive override than predictive driver. | N (reactive only)
5 | Token-per-request (TPR) shift detection | Workload change detector | Request logs / model telemetry | deployment_id | 5m | 10–30 min | 4 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 5.5 | Hard to separate real shift vs sampling; high-cardinality data | Useful to adjust capacity per QPS when TPR changes; expensive pipeline. Consider later. | N
6 | Customer upstream “traffic intent” webhook | External signal | Customer emits forecast/intent | deployment_id | customer-defined | 5–240 min | 2 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 6.0 | Integration burden; trust boundary; support overhead | Could be powerful for a small set of enterprise customers; requires auth, schemas, retries. | N (phase 2/pilot-only)
7 | Calendar holidays / region events | Global schedule | Public holiday calendar + region mapping | region | annual | 1–7 days | 3 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 6.0 | Wrong for most B2B; varies by customer business | Low effort add-on once seasonal baseline exists, but not MVP-critical. | N
8 | Marketing/product launch annotations (internal) | Manual annotation | Customer success / TAM notes | account_id | ad hoc | 1–30 days | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 1.5 | Not scalable; stale; not auditable | Avoid building into system; treat as playbook item. | N
9 | Smart routing “spillover risk” / capacity pressure | Platform signal | Fleet capacity planner + routing | region + hw_type | 1–5m | 5–30 min | 4 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 7.5 | Conflates multi-tenant pressure; Dedicated isolation caveats | Might be useful only to choose “how aggressive to pre-scale” when region tight; keep separate from demand forecast. | N
10 | Historical p95 latency early-warning | Derived metric | Request latency metrics | deployment_id | 1m | 1–10 min | 5 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 6.0 | Latency may rise after queue already present; noisy | Better as reactive override / safety signal (don’t wait for forecast). | N
11 | Reservation utilization (GPU saturation) | Platform metric | GPU telemetry | deployment_id + node | 10–30s | 0–5 min | 5 | 4 | 2 | 1 | 9.5 | Good reactive control; not truly predictive | Keep in reactive loop; can be combined with forecast for arbitration. | N
12 | “Known daily ramp” detector (auto-enroll) | Meta-signal | Analyzer over historical QPS | deployment_id | weekly | 30–120 min | 4 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 8.5 | False positives; customers surprised by behavior | Could drive recommendation (“enable predictive schedule”) rather than automatic behavior in MVP. | N (recommendation only)

MVP recommendation (phase 1)
1) Seasonal baseline forecast (time-of-day/day-of-week)
- Why: broad coverage, reliable, strong for predictable ramps (Hexagon-style). Low enough complexity to ship.
- Guardrails: staleness checks, conservative confidence, clamp within min/max, cooldown/dampening.

2) Scheduled events (customer-configured)
- Why: gives customers direct control for known ramps (batch jobs, ETL, daily open). Also reduces “we don’t trust your ML” objections.
- Guardrails: RBAC + audit logs, validation, rate limits on changes.

3) Trend extrapolation fallback (EMA)
- Why: still helps when patterns shift or the seasonal model is cold; minimal pipeline work.
- Guardrails: treat as minor bias only; let reactive saturation override.

Phase 2 candidates
- Customer traffic intent webhook (enterprise-only), after we harden semantics/support.
- Automatic ramp detector (but as “recommendation surfaced in Console” rather than auto-enroll).
- Token-per-request shift detector (if we see real incidents driven by workload mix changes).

Signals explicitly not recommended as “predictive driver”
- Queue depth as predictive driver: too close to reactive, model/batching sensitivity (see Slack thread eng-runtime/1749044307). Keep as reactive override.
- Marketing/internal annotations: doesn’t scale, poor auditability.

Data availability / pipeline notes (implementation reality check)
- Minimum viable forecast needs: per deployment_id + region metrics for QPS + tokens/sec (or tokens/min).
- Retention needed: at least 2–4 weeks for stable DOW patterns; for new deployments we will be in “cold start mode” (seasonal forecast disabled; use EMA + reactive).
- Timezone: MUST be explicit. Proposal: scaling_policy.timezone required if predictive enabled; default UTC but UI warns; store as IANA tz string (e.g., America/Chicago).
- Staleness: if forecast age > 2x refresh interval or missing for > N minutes => disable predictive contribution and emit metric + event.

Operational risks / safety notes
- Oscillation: worst case when forecast overshoots then reactive sees low utilization and scales down aggressively. Mitigation: cooldowns + “hold” periods + minimum step sizes.
- Max bound saturation: forecast can’t help if max too low; need clear observability (“bounded at max” vs “predictor wrong”).
- Region capacity shortages (min unmet): predictive demand doesn’t matter if supply constrained; surface degraded state and alert.

Open questions
- What is the forecast output we want to standardize on?
  - Option A: desired_replicas (direct)
  - Option B: desired_tokens_per_sec and we translate using current perf model
  - Current leaning: output desired_replicas per deployment/region to keep loop simple; revisit once perf models are consistent.
- Confidence: do we need a numeric confidence now, or just binary “available/unavailable”? Leaning: numeric (0–1) but only used to scale contribution, not exposed to customers in v1.
- Aggregation: do we forecast on QPS, tokens/sec, or concurrency? Leaning: tokens/sec as primary, QPS as secondary sanity check.

Next steps
- Sana: define evaluation KPIs for forecast quality (MAPE on tokens/sec; “ramp miss” count; overshoot cost).
- Mei: prototype DOW x 5-min seasonal baseline on 6 pilot traces; report PI deltas vs EMA-only.
- Vanessa/Keiko: confirm lead-time requirements for scale-up in Dedicated (GPU warmup, model load), so we can set minimum “forecast horizon” to be useful.
- Align with ENG-22142 on the provider interface: required fields should include timestamp, horizon, staleness, and (optional) confidence.

Change log
- 2025-06-12: initial draft list (Mei)
- 2025-06-20: added scheduled events + webhook option after customer calls (Sana)
- 2025-07-02: reweighted scoring and marked MVP set (Vanessa feedback)
